cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Hi. Can I help you?

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: I’d like to find out if you have any excursions suitable for families.

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Sure. How about taking your family for a cruise? We have a steamship that takes passengers out several times a day (Example) - it’s over 100 years old.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: That sounds interesting. How long is the trip?

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: About an hour and a half. And don’t forget to take pictures of the mountains (Q1). They’re all around you when you’re on the boat and they look fantastic.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: OK. And I assume there’s a café or something on board?

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Sure. How old are your children?

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: Er, my daughter’s fifteen and my son’s seven.

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Right. Well there are various things you can do once you’ve crossed the lake, to make a day of it. One thing that’s very popular is a visit to the Country Farm. You’re met off the boat by the farmer and he’ll take you to the holding pens, where the sheep are kept. Children love feeling them!

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: My son would love that. He really likes animals.

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Well, there’s also a 40-minute trek round the farm on a horse (Q2), if he wants.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: Do you think he’d manage it? He hasn’t done that before.

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Sure. It’s suitable for complete beginners.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: Ah, good.

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: And again, visitors are welcome to explore the farm on their own, as long as they take care to close gates and so on. There are some very beautiful gardens along the side of the lake which also belong to the farm (Q3) - they’ll be just at their best now. You could easily spend an hour or two there.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: OK. Well that all sounds good. And can we get lunch there? (Q4)

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: You can, and it’s very good, though it’s not included in the basic cost. You pay when you get there.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: So is there anything else to do over on that side of the lake?

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Well, what you can do is take a bike over on the ship and then go on a cycling trip. There’s a trail there called the Back Road - you could easily spend three or four hours exploring it, and the scenery’s wonderful. They’ll give you a map when you get your ticket for the cruise - there’s no extra charge. (Q5)

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: What’s the trail like in terms of difficulty?

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Quite challenging in places. It wouldn’t be suitable for your seven-year-old. It needs someone who’s got a bit more experience. (Q6)

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: Hmm. Well, my daughter loves cycling and so do I, so maybe the two of us could go, and my wife and son could stay on the farm. That might work out quite well. But we don’t have bikes here… is there somewhere we could rent them?

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Yes, there’s a place here in the city. It’s called Ratchesons. (Q7)

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: I’ll just make a note of that - er, how do you spell it?

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: R-A-T-C-H-E-S-O-N-S. It’s just be the cruise ship terminal.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: OK.

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: You’d also need to pick up a repair kit for the bike from there to take along with you, and you’d need to take along a snack and some water - it’d be best to get those in the city.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: Fine. That shouldn’t be a problem. And I assume I can rent a helmet from the bike place? (Q8)

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Sure, you should definitely get that. It’s a great ride, but you want to be well prepared because it’s very remote - you won’t see any shops round there, or anywhere to stay (Q9), so you need to get back in time for the last boat.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: Yeah. So what sort of prices are we looking at here?

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Let’s see, that’d be one adult and one child for the cruise with farm tour, that’s $117, and an adult and a child for the cruise only so that’s $214 dollars altogether. Oh, wait a minute, how old did you say your daughter was?

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: Fifteen.

cues.speaker: TC EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Then I’m afraid it’s $267 (Q10) because she has to pay the adult fare, which is $75 instead of the child fare which is $22 - sorry about that.

cues.speaker: VISITOR
cues.text: That’s OK. Er, so how do …
